Lessons.Title: Connecting Equations to Graphs (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: rearrange ax+by=c to y=mx+b, calculate slope and y-intercept, and explain their meaning using more than one equation form. Independently authored Edulytiks material aligned to Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U02:L11, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/2/11/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). Building On 6.EE.A.3 and 8.EE.B; Addressing HSA-CED.A.4 and HSA-REI.D.10.

Independent example: 3x+2y=18. Isolating y gives y=9−1.5x, so slope is −3/2 and intercept (0,9); x-intercept (6,0). The line represents all real pairs satisfying the original equation. In a context with whole-number items, only feasible integer coordinates apply.

Second original example: 5y+10x=40 gives y=8−2x, which makes the y-intercept 8 and change rate −2 visible. Difference between the two forms: standard form helps identify a fixed total, slope-intercept reveals rate and initial value.

Student task: graph two independently authored lines, rewrite their equations without changing the solution sets, test two points per line and explain an off-graph pair. Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, max 8): valid isolation, numerical slope/intercepts, graph/scale, and contextual explanation with verified substitution.

KeyConcepts.Title: Standard form
KeyConcepts.Definition: ax+by=c hides some graphical features until rearranged.

KeyConcepts.Title: Slope
KeyConcepts.Definition: Rate of change is Δy/Δx; standard-form slope is −a/b for b≠0.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use two known points as independent check.

KeyConcepts.Title: Intercept
KeyConcepts.Definition: An intercept occurs where the other coordinate is zero.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Set x or y to zero in the original equation.

WorkedExamples.Title: Rearrange a standard form
WorkedExamples.Question: Write 3x+2y=18 in slope-intercept form.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
Steps: Read intercept b=9 and slope m=−3/2.
WorkedExamples.Check: Both equation forms share exactly the same real solution pairs.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find slope from intercepts
WorkedExamples.Question: Find the slope and intercepts of 5y+10x=40.
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check a proposed point
WorkedExamples.Question: Is (2,6) on the graph 3x+2y=18?
WorkedExamples.Method: Explain each mathematical move and verify the result in the original equations.
Steps: Left equals right, so the point is on the line.
Read it as a pair of real solutions, before applying any context.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dividing only one term in 18−3x by 2
Assuming standard form slope is a/b

SummaryPoints: Equivalent equation forms emphasize different features of the same line.
Intercepts follow by setting the other variable to zero.
Students must explain graph points and rate, not only calculate numbers.
